title: Juz' 'Amma, the shape
hook: thirty-seven surahs: the Day, the orphan, the soul, the One

segments.voice: Yesterday, the end of An-Naba': the Day of fasl, when what was mixed is separated. Your line was the day of sorting. What did you choose to send ahead? Day two hundred twenty-two.

When you finish a hike, there's a moment near the top when you turn around. The path you climbed is all laid out below you, and for the first time you can see its shape: where it switched back, where it got steep, where you stopped for water. Since day one hundred fifty-nine we've been walking backward through the last part of the Qur'an, from An-Nas on its final page to An-Naba' at the front. Yesterday we reached the start. So today we don't read a new surah. We turn around and look at the whole thing. Thirty-seven surahs, and four things they keep coming back to. Today: Juz' 'Amma, the shape.
screen: `TURNING AROUND NEAR THE TOP.` → `FROM AN-NAS BACK TO AN-NABA'.` → `THE WHOLE PATH IN VIEW.`

segments.voice: First, what a juz' is. Juz' means a part. The Qur'an's surahs are of very different lengths, and later Muslims divided the text into thirty parts of roughly equal length, so it could be read in a month, a part a day, as some do in Ramadan. The division is a reading aid, not part of the revelation itself. The thirtieth part runs from Surah seventy-eight to the end, thirty-seven surahs, and it's named for its first word, 'amma, about what. They're short, they rhyme, and several open with oaths: by the dawn, by the sun, by the fig and the olive. And under all that sound, four themes keep returning. The Day: An-Naba', Az-Zalzalah, Al-Qari'ah, the sorting and the weighing. The orphan: again and again the surahs ask who fed the orphan and who pushed him away, from Ad-Duha to Al-Ma'un. The soul: Ash-Shams swears by the soul and the One who shaped it, and says whoever purifies it has succeeded. And the One: Al-Ikhlas, four short lines on the oneness of Allah. The Day, the orphan, the soul, the One. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ came from an orphan's childhood himself, which gives the orphan verses a sound all their own. It's often the first part children learn by heart: short enough to hold, one surah at a time, and full of those four things.
screen: `JUZ' — ONE OF THIRTY PARTS.` · `THIRTY-SEVEN SHORT SURAHS.` · `THE DAY, THE ORPHAN, THE SOUL, THE ONE.` · `OFTEN LEARNED FIRST, BY HEART.` · then, large: `THE WHOLE JUZ'.`

segments.voice: Sit, and let the last few weeks come back to you, one surah at a time. The whisperer that withdraws. Daybreak. Say, He is Allah, the One. The morning light of Ad-Duha. The man who frowned. The trumpet and the crowds. Don't try to remember them all. Just notice which ones come back on their own, the ones that stuck. Pick three. Hold their names in your mind, and ask yourself what each one gave you. The bell holds the time.
Juz' 'Amma. The thirtieth part of the Qur'an, thirty-seven surahs named for their first word: the Day, the orphan, the soul, the One. Today's word.
Your line: the whole juz'. Today, write down your three favorite surahs from this part, and one line about why each one stayed with you. Day two hundred twenty-two.

howItsDone: Muslim children often learn Juz' 'Amma first, starting from its end (An-Nas) and working backward, and its short surahs are commonly recited in the daily prayers; the thirty-part division lets a reader finish the whole Qur'an across a month, as some do in Ramadan.

original.note: Arabic: the part of 'amma, named for the first word of Surah 78.

trapdoor: what you thought: the last chapter of the Qur'an.
what it means: the thirtieth of thirty reading parts, thirty-seven short surahs on the Day, the orphan, the soul and the One.
what a scholar hears: the juz' division is post-prophetic, for reading; the standard edition's headings class nearly all of these surahs as Meccan.

notes: Editor review (2026-10-01): cut unsourced claims: 'so many people finish the Qur'an in Ramadan', 'most of these surahs are Meccan, from the early years', 'many open with oaths', 'the part children usually memorize first' and 'most often heard in the prayers' (tomorrow's topic); empty 'deep enough to keep for life' replaced; screen heads and howItsDone/myth/fork softened to match.
The statement that the thirty-part division is a later reading aid (not part of the revelation) reflects standard accounts; confirm phrasing.
Assumes the camp read the juz' from An-Nas backward starting day 159; confirm against the outline for the recap in the hook and practice.
Classification of these surahs as mostly Meccan follows the standard Cairo edition headings; a few (e.g. al-Bayyinah, an-Nasr) are usually counted Medinan, which is why the script says 'most'.
